alignments.note: Rule 21's determinerless clause: the case preposition *at* rides with the noun, the ASV supplying no determiner for an article to anchor.

The genitive absolute's participle has no English word of its own: the ASV compresses Ὀψίας γενομένης into the bare temporal phrase *at even*, which I gave whole to the noun under rule 21. Stretching *at* onto the participle instead would leave the noun without its case preposition.
Rule 9: the periphrastic auxiliary *did* rides with the verb, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 9: subject rides with the verb.
Rule 90: the ASV writes one English word for the substantival article before its participle, and that word is the pronoun-cum-relativizer the article takes; the participle keeps its own verb.
Adverb; rule 2 splits it from its verb, the ASV spelling both elements out.
Participle rendered by the copula of the English predicate.
Rule 32: the substantival article supplies the pronoun and nothing else, the ASV writing a separate *them* here.

Rule 32: the relativizer and copula are the participle's helpers. Head corrected from *possessed* to *demons*: δαιμονίζομαι is a denominative verb whose lexeme is the δαιμον- root, and rule 91's operational test asks which English word the corpus spends on that root — `δαιμόνιον` → *demons* at 1:34 and 1:39 of this chapter — while *possessed* is the generic verb the ASV supplies to make an English clause, as *moved* is at 1:41 and *sick* at 1:30. Rules 17 and 66 agree, the meaning-bearing complement being the head in a support rendering. The competing reading heads on *possessed* as the English predicate's own lexical verb, which is defensible on rule 91's `βλασφημέω` → *speaking evil* precedent; I took the root-noun reading because there the verb word *speaking* is itself the φημ- root, whereas here no part of *possessed* answers to δαιμον-.

review_notes: The two substantival articles are treated differently because the ASV writes one English word for the first (rule 90) and two for the second (rule 32).
γενομένης is left `unrepresented`; its unit's note records why *at even* was kept whole on Ὀψίας. A reference comparison reports it as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

Reconciliation: the target head of δαιμονιζομένους moved from *possessed* to *demons*, bringing this unit into line with 1:41 σπλαγχνισθείς → *compassion* and 1:30 πυρέσσουσα → *fever*, which are the same construction. Unit membership is unchanged and no other unit in the verse is touched.
